stimuli.text: A block of mass 4 kg on a 20° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 5 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.1. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.2 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.19\cos(11t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A hoop (I = MR²) and a solid cylinder (I = ½MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2.8 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 35° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Friction acts up the slope.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.

questions.stem: A curve of radius 120 m is banked so that a car at 27 m/s needs no friction. What is the banking angle?

options.why: Correct. tan θ = v²/(rg).
Use tan θ = v²/(rg), from dividing the force components.
Square the speed.
Measure the angle from the horizontal.

questions.stem: A boat points straight across a river 40 m wide, moving at 3 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 2 m/s. How long does the crossing take?

options.why: The current is perpendicular to the heading.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.
The perpendicular component alone sets the crossing time.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 1x$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 2$$ m?

options.why: Correct. W = ∫F dx.
The force is not constant.
Divide by n + 1 when integrating.
Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.16\cos(5t)$$ m. What is its maximum acceleration?

options.why: That is v_max.
Differentiate twice: Aω².
Correct. a_max = Aω².
Multiply by the amplitude.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 20 m high at 14 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Take the square root for the time.
Recheck the fall time.
Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Fall time is √(2h/g).

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 0.7 m swings about a pivot at one end with small amplitude. What is its period?

options.why: Correct. T = 2π√(I/(mgd)) with I = mL²/3 and d = L/2.
d is L/2, the distance to the center of mass.
I = mL²/3.
A rod is a physical pendulum, not a simple one.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 410 kg load 27 m at constant speed in 11 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: P = W/t.
Correct. P = mgh/t.
Include g.
That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A 2 kg cart moving at 3 m/s collides with and sticks to a 1 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.
The carts share the momentum.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.

questions.explanation: v_f = 2·3/3 = 2 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 3 J.

questions.stem: A 4 kg ball moving at +3 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 5 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 5 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Kinetic energy is conserved too.
Only equal masses exchange velocities.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -0.333 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 2.67 m/s.

questions.stem: A 2500 kg car heading east at 9 m/s collides with a 1000 kg car heading north at 11 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Weight each velocity by its mass.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Divide by the total mass.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 43 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 17 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.
Recheck the average.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.

questions.stem: A 6 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 4t^2$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: The force is not constant.
Integrate the force over time.
Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
Divide by the mass to get speed.

questions.stem: A planet has 4 times Earth's mass and 0.5 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)

options.why: g depends on 1/R², not 1/R.
g decreases with radius.
Correct. g ∝ M/R².
The ratio is inverted.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 470$$ N/m is compressed 0.11 m and launches a 0.1 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: Take the square root.
The ½ appears on both sides.
Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).

questions.stem: Masses of 4 kg and 3 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the tension in the string?

options.why: The heavier mass accelerates down, so T is less than its weight.
The lighter mass accelerates up, so T exceeds its weight.
Correct. T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂).
Use T = m₂(g + a).

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -9x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: T = 2π/ω, not 2πω.
Correct. ω = √9 = 3 rad/s, T = 2π/ω.
ω is the square root of the coefficient.
T = 2π/ω.

questions.stem: A car moving at 6 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 5 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.
Divide by 2a, not a.
That is the stopping time in seconds.
Δx = v₀²/(2a).

questions.stem: A 58 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating upward at 4 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: Include gravity.
Check the direction of the acceleration.
The acceleration changes the normal force.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).

questions.stem: A 0.2 kg ball hits a wall at 16 m/s and rebounds at 4 m/s. The contact lasts 0.03 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: Include the rebound.
The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.
Divide by time.

questions.stem: A 1 kg ball on a 0.6 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 8 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Centripetal force uses v².
Include gravity.
Correct. At the top, T + mg = mv²/r.
Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 4 kg and radius 0.4 m spins at 15 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 1 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Use rotational inertias, not masses.
The clay's inertia is mR².
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.

questions.stem: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 3.2 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: That is only correct for a hoop.
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².
Some energy goes into rotation.
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ½MR².

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 11 rad/s and amplitude 0.18 m. What is its speed when it is 0.072 m from equilibrium?

options.why: Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.
That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Use A² − x² under a square root.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 6x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 2$$ m?

options.why: Divide by n + 1 when integrating.
Integrate; do not just evaluate F.
The force is not constant.
Correct. W = ∫F dx.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 4 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?

options.why: Farther satellites move more slowly.
Correct. v = √(GM/r), so v ∝ r^(−1/2).

questions.stem: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 2 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Some energy goes into rotation.
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ½MR².
That is only correct for a hoop.
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².

questions.stem: A 2 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 8 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
I/R² = M/2.
The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
For a disk, I/R² = M/2.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 3.27 m/s².

questions.stem: An object of mass 1 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.02$$ kg/s. What is its terminal speed?

options.why: That is the time constant.
Solve mg = bv for v.
Correct. At terminal speed, mg = bv.
Drag here is linear in v.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 490 m/s and τ = m/b = 50 s.

questions.stem: A 8 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 5 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.2. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Friction opposes the motion.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.
Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.
Include friction on the table block.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 1.2 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
The weight acts at L/2.
τ = MgL/2.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$2 \times 10^{25}$$ kg and radius $$5 \times 10^{6}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: Take the square root.
Correct. ½mv² = GMm/R.
Potential energy uses 1/R.
That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^3$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The rod is not uniform.
Integrate x·xⁿ and xⁿ correctly.
Correct. x_cm = ∫xλ dx / ∫λ dx.
The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: A uniform 6 m beam weighing 300 N rests on supports at both ends. A 600 N load sits 2 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 2 m down a 37° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.3. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction removes energy.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 5t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 4 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its velocity at $$t = 5$$ s?

options.why: Integrating tⁿ divides by n + 1.
The acceleration is not constant, so constant-acceleration equations do not apply.
Correct. Integrate a(t) and add the initial velocity.
Include the initial velocity.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 4x^3 - 27x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
Take the square root.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
dU/dx = 3ax² − b.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 12x² − 27 = 0 gives x = 1.5 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 10 m/s at 70° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its time of flight?

options.why: That is the time to the top; the flight is twice as long.
Use the vertical component.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
Use v₀ sin θ.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 3.42 m/s, v₀y = 9.4 m/s. T = 2v₀y/g = 1.92 s.

questions.stem: What is the rotational inertia of a uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 1 m about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?

options.why: That is about the center.
The mass is spread along the rod.
That is a disk's formula.
Correct. I = ML²/3 (parallel-axis theorem from ML²/12).

questions.stem: A 24 g bullet moving at 330 m/s embeds in a 2.4 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.
h = V²/(2g).
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.

questions.explanation: V = 3.27 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.545 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 4 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 0.5 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.19 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
